outcome: Urethrovesical junction (UVJ) mobility (retrovesical angle (RVA) and pubovesical angle (PVA))
cohort: 217 pregnant women during their first pregnancy and 42 controls
finding: Pregnant women had increased UVJ mobility compared to controls, and while both vaginal delivery and cesarean section impact UVJ mobility, women who underwent vaginal delivery had a slower return to pre-pregnancy levels compared to those who had a cesarean section.
mod_finding: Women who underwent vaginal delivery had significantly higher PVA 6 weeks postpartum compared to women who underwent cesarean section.
